forbes_bio: Michael Dell is chairman and CEO of Dell Technologies, which formed in 2016 via Dell's $60 billion merger with computer storage giant EMC.
Dell Technologies returned to public markets through a complicated financial restructuring in 2018 after Dell and private equity firm Silver Lake Partners took it private in 2013.
Dell's cloud software arm, VMware, spun off in 2021; Microchip firm Broadcom bought it in 2023 for $69 billion, 39% of which went to Dell.
Much of Dell's fortune lies in his private investment firm DFO Management, which has stakes in hotels and invests in liquid corporate credit.
In 2025, Dell and his wife committed $6.25 billion to seed investment accounts for 25 million U.S. children with $250 apiece.
forbes_facts: Dell got his start at 19 selling computers out of his University of Texas dorm room, grossing $80,000 by the end of his freshman year.
Dell's DFO Management owns the Four Seasons Maui, plus indirect stakes in Applebees, IHOP, Calvin Klein and reportedly Grand Central Station.

name: Guillermo Rauch
forbes_bio: Guillermo Rauch cofounded Vercel, which creates developer tools for hosting and deploying websites.
In September 2025, the company raised $300 million, co-led by venture firm Accel and GIC, one of Singapore's sovereign wealth funds, putting Vercel's valuation at $9 billion.
Rauch, an Argentine immigrant to the U.S., became famous in the developer community as a teen, after becoming a core contributor to MooTools, a popular Javascript library.
Vercel has become a crucial infrastructure vendor for some of the world's biggest brands, including Under Armour, Stripe and Sonos.
forbes_facts: One of the most popular ways to view the Epstein Files, an interface called Jmail that mimics a Gmail inbox, is hosted on Vercel.

name: Oleg Misrevra
forbes_bio: Oleg Misevra controls East Mining Company, a Russian thermal coal enterprise.
Misevra, who served the Internal Troops of USSR and Russia, became a top manager and minority partner of the MDM Group, A WHATKT in the early 2000s.
MDM was founded by Andrey Melnichenko and Sergey Popov, who both became billionaires buying industrial plants across Russia.
In 2002, Misevra was elected as president of the Siberian Coal Energy Company (SUEK), the largest Russian thermal coal producer.
He resigned as president of SUEK in 2004 and purchased the company's assets on Sakhalin Island.
